_meta.author: Andrei Sidorenko 5750779
_meta.description: Chief of Police hint lines. Object hints fire when the player is near an interactable object. Room unlock hints will fire when a locked room is unlocked.
_meta.status: All 7 rooms covered. 13 object hints, 4 NPC greetings, 31 suspect reactions, 3 room unlock hints, 3 endings.

object_hint.case_file:
This is the document of the case you're working on.
Elena, a married woman with kids, prominent researcher
and professor at the city university, has been found dead
in her office at 11:47 PM.
object_hint.computer:
A draft email on the screen — addressed to a lawyer.
The subject line reads: 'Regarding financial irregularities
in Dean Osei's department.' The draft is unfinished.
object_hint.tweed_thread: The lamp is smashed. There's a small thread caught on the broken edge — coarse, woven, looks like tweed.
object_hint.dinner_invitation:
A faculty dinner invitation for last night.
We should check what time it actually ended.
object_hint.accusation_board: The board's almost empty. We need solid evidence before we can put a name on it. Keep digging.
object_hint.map_board: The case map. Every location and connection we know so far. Useful for tracking who was where.
object_hint.research_paper: A draft research paper. Elena is listed as the sole author. Another name has been crossed out in red — Lena Voss.
object_hint.keyboard: Security station keyboard. Could pull up the CCTV logs from here — if anyone bothered to keep them running.
object_hint.master_key_log: Master key log from last night. Two people have keys: Dean Osei and the head of security. One of these keys was used at 11:18 PM.
object_hint.phone: Phone log on the screen. A call placed at 10:55 PM — 0 seconds, no answer. The receiving number is Elena's.
object_hint.divorce_agreement: Divorce paperwork. Custody hearing next month. Elena was applying to move Sophie to Switzerland.
object_hint.laptop: Victor's laptop on the desk. Locked — it wants a numeric password.
object_hint.jacket: A tweed jacket on the rack. There's a small tear on the left sleeve. The colour and weave look familiar.

npc_greeting.marcus: That's Marcus, Elena's ex-husband. Let's talk to him.
npc_greeting.victor: That's Dean Osei. We should talk to him.
npc_greeting.lena: That's Lena Voss — Elena's research partner. Let's see what she has to say.
npc_greeting.waiter: The waiter who worked the dinner that night. He'd know exactly when it ended.

tweed_thread_to_marcus.speaker: marcus
tweed_thread_to_marcus.text: Tweed? I don't own anything tweed. That's more Victor's style — he wears that jacket everywhere.

tweed_thread_to_marcus.speaker: chief
tweed_thread_to_marcus.text: Notice who he's pointing the finger at. Doesn't mean he's right — but it's worth remembering.

tweed_thread_to_lena.speaker: lena
tweed_thread_to_lena.text: That looks like the dean's jacket. Victor always wears that tweed. Elena used to joke about it.

tweed_thread_to_lena.speaker: chief
tweed_thread_to_lena.text: That's two people now placing this kind of jacket on the same person. Independent of each other.

tweed_thread_to_victor.speaker: victor
tweed_thread_to_victor.text: A thread? Could be from anyone. The university dry-cleans dozens of jackets.

tweed_thread_to_victor.speaker: chief
tweed_thread_to_victor.text: He didn't deny it's his. And he just touched his left sleeve.

master_key_log_to_marcus.speaker: marcus
master_key_log_to_marcus.text: The master key was used during the murder? You should be talking to Victor, not me.

master_key_log_to_lena.speaker: lena
master_key_log_to_lena.text: Only Victor and security have master keys. I always thought it was strange the dean had one.

master_key_log_to_lena.speaker: chief
master_key_log_to_lena.text: Lena's keycard was logged at the lab, not Elena's office. A keycard like hers wouldn't have opened that door anyway.

master_key_log_to_victor.speaker: victor
master_key_log_to_victor.text: The head of security must have done a routine check.

master_key_log_to_victor.speaker: detective
master_key_log_to_victor.text: The head of security was off duty. I checked.

master_key_log_to_victor.speaker: victor
master_key_log_to_victor.text: I… think I should speak with my solicitor.

master_key_log_to_victor.speaker: chief
master_key_log_to_victor.text: He's shutting down. Whatever the answer was, it wasn't 'routine check'.

computer_to_marcus.speaker: marcus
computer_to_marcus.text: Financial irregularities? She never told me. But she always said Victor was dodgy.

computer_to_marcus.speaker: chief
computer_to_marcus.text: Marcus seems genuinely unaware. Whatever Elena was investigating, it wasn't through him.

computer_to_lena.speaker: lena
computer_to_lena.text: She told me she found something in the grant accounts. She said people could go to prison.

computer_to_lena.speaker: chief
computer_to_lena.text: Lena's heard about it. Elena was talking to her about something serious — serious enough to put people in prison.

computer_to_victor.speaker: victor
computer_to_victor.text: Elena had strong opinions about budget allocation.

computer_to_victor.speaker: detective
computer_to_victor.text: Fake vendor invoices are hard to misunderstand.

computer_to_victor.speaker: victor
computer_to_victor.text: I'm not commenting without my solicitor.

computer_to_victor.speaker: chief
computer_to_victor.text: He didn't deny it. Deflected again.

case_file_to_marcus.speaker: marcus
case_file_to_marcus.text: I already gave my statement. What more do you want?

case_file_to_marcus.speaker: chief
case_file_to_marcus.text: This just has the basic facts. It won't provoke much of a reaction. Try showing something more specific.

case_file_to_lena.speaker: lena
case_file_to_lena.text: I've read this already. It doesn't tell me anything I don't know.

case_file_to_lena.speaker: chief
case_file_to_lena.text: This just has the basic facts. It won't provoke much of a reaction. Try showing something more specific.

case_file_to_victor.speaker: victor
case_file_to_victor.text: A tragic case. Elena was a brilliant researcher. Terrible loss for the university.

case_file_to_victor.speaker: chief
case_file_to_victor.text: This just has the basic facts. It won't provoke much of a reaction. Try showing something more specific.

divorce_agreement_to_marcus.speaker: marcus
divorce_agreement_to_marcus.text: That's right. She wanted everything. Sophie too — moving her to bloody Switzerland. But wanting someone gone isn't the same as killing them, detective.

divorce_agreement_to_marcus.speaker: chief
divorce_agreement_to_marcus.text: He admits the resentment openly. Make of that what you will.

waiter_testimony.speaker: waiter
waiter_testimony.text: The faculty dinner? Finished around quarter to eleven. The dean in the tweed jacket left right away.

waiter_testimony.speaker: chief
waiter_testimony.text: Quarter to eleven. Keep that in mind — it doesn't quite match what we were told earlier.

marcus_introduction.speaker: marcus
marcus_introduction.text: Detective. I already told the officers everything I know. I was home that night. Alone. I had nothing to do with what happened to Elena.

marcus_introduction.speaker: marcus
marcus_introduction.text: Look — yes, the divorce was ugly. Yes, the custody fight is ongoing. But whoever did this... it wasn't me. You should be looking at Victor. He never liked her either.

marcus_introduction.speaker: chief
marcus_introduction.text: Bitter, defensive, points the finger elsewhere. Standard. But he hasn't given us anything we can verify or disprove.

victor_introduction.speaker: victor
victor_introduction.text: Detective Rowe. Terrible business about Elena. Please, sit. Can I offer you tea?

victor_introduction.speaker: victor
victor_introduction.text: I was at the faculty dinner until quite late. After that, straight home. I'm happy to answer anything that might help your investigation.

victor_introduction.speaker: chief
victor_introduction.text: Composed, charming, helpful — almost rehearsed. Watch what he doesn't say.

lena_introduction.speaker: lena
lena_introduction.text: Detective. I... I already gave my statement to the officers. I was in the lab until eleven, then home. My keycard will show it.

lena_introduction.speaker: lena
lena_introduction.text: Elena and I had our disagreements about the research paper, yes. But she was my friend, before all that. I would never... I couldn't.

lena_introduction.speaker: chief
lena_introduction.text: Nervous, defensive, but she's not hiding her alibi — she's volunteering it. Either she's telling the truth or she's very prepared.

tweed_thread_to_waiter.speaker: waiter
tweed_thread_to_waiter.text: A piece of fabric? I'm just the waiter, sir. I clean tables. I wouldn't know anything about clothes.

master_key_log_to_waiter.speaker: waiter
master_key_log_to_waiter.text: Keys to what? I have my locker key and a key to the kitchen. That's all I need.

case_file_to_waiter.speaker: waiter
case_file_to_waiter.text: Oh, I read about it in the papers. Awful thing. But I really only know what I saw at the dinner.

dinner_invitation_to_waiter.speaker: waiter
dinner_invitation_to_waiter.text: Yes, that's the dinner from last night. We had it from eight until quarter to eleven, like I said.

dinner_invitation_to_waiter.speaker: chief
dinner_invitation_to_waiter.text: He's consistent. Same time every time we ask.

research_paper_to_waiter.speaker: waiter
research_paper_to_waiter.text: Academic papers, sir? I just serve the food. I leave the reading to the professors.

divorce_agreement_to_waiter.speaker: waiter
divorce_agreement_to_waiter.text: Personal matter, isn't it? I don't think I should be looking at this.

divorce_agreement_to_lena.speaker: lena
divorce_agreement_to_lena.text: I... I know things were difficult between Marcus and Elena. Elena mentioned the custody fight once or twice. But it's their private matter.

divorce_agreement_to_lena.speaker: chief
divorce_agreement_to_lena.text: Lena's uncomfortable but not surprised. She knew more than she lets on.

divorce_agreement_to_victor.speaker: victor
divorce_agreement_to_victor.text: Ah yes — Marcus and Elena's divorce. Messy, even by academic standards. But I'd rather not gossip about a colleague's personal life.

divorce_agreement_to_victor.speaker: chief
divorce_agreement_to_victor.text: Smooth deflection. He didn't say he doesn't know about it.

dinner_invitation_to_marcus.speaker: marcus
dinner_invitation_to_marcus.text: A faculty dinner? I'm an ex-husband, not faculty. I wasn't there. I was at home.

dinner_invitation_to_marcus.speaker: chief
dinner_invitation_to_marcus.text: Marcus is quick to remind us where he was. He hasn't been asked.

dinner_invitation_to_lena.speaker: lena
dinner_invitation_to_lena.text: I was invited but I didn't go. I had lab work to finish. The keycard logs will show it.

dinner_invitation_to_lena.speaker: chief
dinner_invitation_to_lena.text: Same alibi she gave us on the keycard. Consistent.

dinner_invitation_to_victor.speaker: victor
dinner_invitation_to_victor.text: Yes, I was at the dinner. Wonderful evening. Stayed until quite late, as I mentioned.

dinner_invitation_to_victor.speaker: chief
dinner_invitation_to_victor.text: He's repeating his story without us asking. Most people would just nod.

research_paper_to_marcus.speaker: marcus
research_paper_to_marcus.text: I have no idea what Elena was working on. We hadn't talked properly in months.

research_paper_to_marcus.speaker: chief
research_paper_to_marcus.text: Plausible. He's a history professor, not a biochemist.

research_paper_to_victor.speaker: victor
research_paper_to_victor.text: Elena's work was excellent. Truly groundbreaking. A tragic loss to the field.

research_paper_to_lena.speaker: lena
research_paper_to_lena.text: I... already have my own copy. We were supposed to be co-authors.

research_paper_to_lena.speaker: chief
research_paper_to_lena.text: She still sounds hurt about it. But hurt isn't the same as guilty.

room_unlocks_hint.victors_house: Good — that's enough to bring in Dean Osei for questioning. Let's pay him a visit at his townhouse.
room_unlocks_hint.faculty_dining_hall: The invitation tells us where the dinner was. Let's head over to the Faculty Dining Hall and see what the waiter remembers.
room_unlocks_hint.lenas_apartment: Looks like Lena had reasons to be upset with Elena. Let's go to her apartment and have a word.

ending.justice_served: Victor is arrested. Confronted with the thread, the key log, and the dinner lie, he confesses. Elena's family gets closure. Case closed.
ending.suspect_escapes: Not enough evidence. Victor's solicitor blocks the charges. He shreds documents and flies out of the country. The case goes cold.
ending.wrong_accusation: An innocent person arrested. Victor walks free. Six months later, new evidence surfaces — but Victor has disappeared. Injustice.
